description: Music Years 9-10 width tiers — ACARA v9. All strands are capability strands; width axis is task_contexts throughout.
subject: Music

width_notes.minimum_width: The narrowest single musical context that honestly satisfies the descriptor's command term. For Y9-10, minimum is typically one stylistically informed task demonstrating the key capability (interpret, compose, develop, reflect, investigate).
width_notes.typical_width: Full descriptor scope across the most common elaboration cases. Reflects a well-taught Y9-10 class engaging with multiple styles, forms, collaborative contexts and critical/reflective practice.
width_notes.wider: Enrichment directions adding new task contexts — different styles, collaborative forms, critical frameworks, technological contexts or social purposes. First Nations contexts included where elaborations indicate them.
width_notes.elaborations: ACARA elaborations used as source data. E02 descriptor is entirely First Nations-focused and its elaborations are the primary framing for that entry.

AC9AMU10C01.minimum_width: Interpret music in one style, applying at least two style-specific vocal or instrumental techniques to communicate a musical intention; demonstrate understanding of relevant elements and compositional devices.
AC9AMU10C01.typical_width: Interpret music across a variety of forms and styles — controlling technical and expressive qualities for accuracy, fluency and stylistic understanding; comparing how elements and compositional devices are used in traditional, digital and graphic scores; identifying and applying stylistic conventions; selecting and practising a performance program around a theme, style or composer.
wider: Select, prepare and present a themed performance program (social, historical or stylistic theme) — research the composers and performers, document stylistic conventions applied, and evaluate the program's coherence
Compare how the same piece is interpreted by multiple performers — analyse how technical and expressive choices differ and how each reflects a different understanding of the composer's intention
Perform in a contrasting style to usual — investigate the conventions, practise the techniques, and reflect on what the stylistic shift required
Perform and record a piece, then compare the recording against a professional version — identify three specific differences and develop a targeted practice plan
elaborations: rehearsing and refining their ability to control technical and expressive qualities in solo and/or ensemble music
experimenting with and comparing how the elements of music and compositional devices are used to communicate musical intentions in traditional, digital or graphic scores
identifying stylistic conventions relevant to music they are learning and practising to apply the conventions in their performance
selecting, interpreting and practising a performance program that focuses on a particular theme, music style or the work of a composer or performer

AC9AMU10C02.minimum_width: Compose a piece in a chosen style, manipulating elements of music and applying at least one style-specific compositional device to communicate an idea; notate, document or record the work.
AC9AMU10C02.typical_width: Compose music across multiple contexts — evaluating how traditions and contexts affect audience response; experimenting with instrumentation, dynamics and texture; working collaboratively on songs or instrumental music (e.g. song cycle, music theatre, film/game music); applying aural understanding of key and tonality; using style-specific compositional devices; analysing elements in a style to use as a guide for arrangement.
wider: Work collaboratively to compose music for a film, animation or video game sequence — make documented decisions about how elements of music serve the narrative or interactive context
Compose a song cycle or set of related pieces exploring an historical or current event — investigate how the chosen style's conventions can carry the theme
Evaluate how different traditions, styles or contexts affect audience response to a piece — use this analysis to compose a new piece designed for a specific audience
Arrange or re-imagine an existing piece by analysing how elements are typically used in the original style, then systematically applying those findings in the new arrangement
elaborations: evaluating how different traditions, styles or contexts affect the way people respond to a piece of music
experimenting with options for using instrumentation, dynamics and expressive techniques to develop the texture of a composition
working collaboratively to compose songs or instrumental music; for example, a song cycle, music theatre work or music for a film, animation or video game
applying an aural understanding of key and tonality when improvising or composing
experimenting with ways to combine and manipulate the elements of music and using style-specific compositional devices
analysing how elements of music are typically used in a music style and using findings as a guide when arranging

AC9AMU10D01.minimum_width: Identify a technically challenging section in music being learnt; develop and apply a targeted practice strategy to improve accuracy and control in that section.
AC9AMU10D01.typical_width: Develop, practise and refine listening/aural skills and style-specific vocal/instrumental skills across solo and ensemble contexts — developing ensemble balance; identifying challenges and building stamina and control; mapping and realising planned dynamic interpretations; systematically extending vocal/instrumental range, fluency, accuracy and expressive facility.
wider: Map a planned dynamic interpretation for a piece using analysis of another performance — identify loudest and softest points, then practise to realise the plan and compare before/after recordings
Develop ensemble skills across multiple ensemble types (e.g. duo, trio and larger ensemble) — compare the listening and balance challenges in each configuration
Undertake a systematic skill-development program to extend vocal or instrumental range — document goals, strategies, progress and reflection over a set period
Work collaboratively to develop ensemble skills by recording and listening back to rehearsals — identify specific balance and intonation issues and develop targeted solutions
elaborations: working collaboratively to develop ensemble skills, such as listening carefully to establish and maintain balance across parts
identifying challenging sections in music they are learning and developing necessary techniques and stamina
mapping a planned approach to interpret dynamics and practising to realise the plan
developing technical and expressive facility and control when using voice and/or instrument/s

AC9AMU10D02.minimum_width: Listen to one example of how another performer interprets a piece; identify one specific technique or expressive choice and explain how it informs their own approach.
AC9AMU10D02.typical_width: Reflect on own and others' music to inform compositional and performance choices — listening and analysing other performers' practices; using scores, charts or lead-sheets to develop interpretations in multiple styles; using aural/memory skills to identify and notate pitch and rhythm patterns, intervals and chord progressions; developing and refining real-time intonation skills.
wider: Listen to multiple interpretations of the same piece by different performers — analyse how each shapes interpretation through technique and expressive choice, then develop a documented personal interpretation
Use aural skills to transcribe a short melody or chord progression by ear — document the process and reflect on what it reveals about the music's structure
Develop real-time intonation skills in ensemble performance — practise identifying and correcting intonation issues while playing, and reflect on how aural awareness improves over time
Build a personal repertoire of identified pitch patterns, intervals and chord progressions through focused listening — use these as a compositional vocabulary in original compositions
elaborations: listening to, analysing and comparing the performance practices of others to shape and refine their own interpretation
using listening, aural skills and understanding of the information provided in scores, charts or lead-sheets to develop interpretations
using focused listening, aural or memory skills to identify, sing or play and/or notate/document music ideas for future use
developing and refining use of aural skills relating to tuning/intonation in real-time performance

AC9AMU10E01.minimum_width: Investigate how one composer or performer uses elements of music, compositional devices or vocal/instrumental techniques in a specific cultural or historical context; describe the effect created and explain the techniques used.
AC9AMU10E01.typical_width: Investigate composers' and performers' use of elements of music across a range of cultures, times and contexts — how composers/performers use elements and devices to influence emotional response; how instrumentation and technique communicate style-specific effects; how music is used in times of conflict and change; how experimental composers combine techniques from different times or cultures; how elements are manipulated in installations or site-specific artworks; how music influences social identity.
wider: Compare how people in different times, places and contexts have used music in times of conflict or social change — analyse what compositional and performative choices carry the message

Investigate 'experimental' composers who combine vocal/instrumental techniques from different cultural or historical contexts — describe what personal style emerges and how it differs from either source tradition
Investigate how elements of music are manipulated in sound designs for site-specific artworks or installations — explore how the space and context shape the music
Analyse how music influences personal or social identity — use this analysis to inform the creation of a new piece designed to create a sense of belonging or community for a specific group
elaborations: investigating ways that composers and/or performers use the elements of music and compositional devices to structure compositions or evoke an emotional response
investigating how composers and performers use instrumentation or instrumental techniques to communicate specific effects
comparing ways that people in a range of times, places and/or other contexts have used music in times of conflict and change
reflecting on why music might be described as 'experimental'
investigating the way elements of music are manipulated in music or sound designs for installations or site-specific artworks
discussing and evaluating the influence of music on the development of personal or social identity
using Viewpoints to ask questions about how technology has changed music styles, composition practices, audiences and the music industry

AC9AMU10E02.minimum_width: Investigate one example of a First Nations Australian performer or composer who celebrates or challenges perspectives of Australian identity through music; describe one specific way the music does this.
AC9AMU10E02.typical_width: Investigate the ways First Nations Australian performers and composers celebrate and challenge multiple perspectives of Australian identity — evaluating innovation in contemporary music including inter-cultural collaborations; investigating how songwriters working in choral, orchestral or chamber music share knowledge, educate, protest or advocate for change; evaluating intentions in music that challenges action on climate change, environmental protection, social justice or racism; mapping First Nations Australian language groups and their music.
wider: Evaluate innovations in contemporary First Nations Australian music including inter-cultural collaborations — describe what is distinctive about the collaborations and what each tradition contributes
Investigate how First Nations Australian songwriters working in diverse genres (e.g. orchestral, chamber, pop) use their music to advocate for specific social or environmental causes

Use an annotated map of First Nations Australian language groups to identify where specific composers and performers are working — research and present short descriptions of two or more artists' music and its cultural context
elaborations: evaluating innovation in the ways that First Nations Australian composers and/or performers are contributing to Australian contemporary music, including inter-cultural collaborations
investigating how First Nations Australian songwriters, performers and/or composers use music to share knowledge, educate, protest, advocate for change or express opinions or beliefs
evaluating intentions/motivations in music that challenges people to take action on issues such as climate change, environmental protection, social justice or racism
using and annotating a map of First Nations Australian language groups to identify where First Nations Australian composers and/or performers are working

AC9AMU10P01.minimum_width: Rehearse and present a planned performance of one piece they have learnt or composed; use at least two style-specific techniques and provide brief information about the music for the audience.
AC9AMU10P01.typical_width: Rehearse and present planned performances across a range of physical or virtual spaces — recording and evaluating using digital tools; performing own compositions with scores or visual material; comparing multiple performances and evaluating which was more successful with audiences; planning performances that include information about the music, performers and intended communication.
wider: Plan and present performances in both physical and virtual spaces — compare how audience interaction and response differ across contexts and reflect on how that shaped performance decisions
Record and systematically evaluate multiple performances of the same piece — identify specific improvements made between performances and document what drove those improvements
Present a performance of original compositions with accompanying scores or visual material — reflect on how the chosen presentation format affected audience understanding and response
Present a themed performance program to a specific audience — provide programme notes for each piece and evaluate how well the program communicated its intended theme or message
elaborations: recording and evaluating performances using digital tools
performing their own music compositions and reflecting on/evaluating personal or audience responses
rehearsing and presenting planned performances, then reflecting on which was more successful with audiences and why
planning and presenting performances in a range of physical or virtual spaces, including providing audiences with information about the music
